title: Every Time Cristiano Ronaldo Snapped (And What Happened Next)

lines: Fourteen red cards. A phone knocked out of a young fan's hand. A microphone thrown into a lake. A captain's armband hurled at the grass.
Cristiano Ronaldo is one of the greatest players of all time. He is also one of the angriest.
Today we go through every time he snapped... why he snapped... and what it cost him after.
His temper is not new. By late twenty twenty-five, ESPN had counted fourteen red cards across his career, for Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus, Al Nassr and Portugal.
One of the ugliest came in January twenty fifteen. Real Madrid away at Córdoba. One all, seven minutes left.
Ronaldo slapped one defender... then kicked out at another, Edimar. Straight red.
On his way off, he pointed at the Club World Cup champions badge on his shirt, right in front of the home fans.
What happened next? A two-match ban, and a public apology to Edimar for what he called his rash act. Real Madrid still won, two one.
June twenty sixteen. The Euros in France. Portugal had drawn their first two games, and Ronaldo had not scored.
On the day of the Hungary game, he is out for a walk by a lake in Lyon. A TV reporter asks if he is ready for the match.
He takes the microphone... and throws it straight into the water.
The reporter worked for a channel Ronaldo had a long feud with. They had covered his private life for years.
No apology. No punishment. And a few weeks later? Portugal won the whole tournament.
September twenty eighteen. His first Champions League game for Juventus, away at Valencia.
In the first half he tangles with defender Jeison Murillo, and appears to pull his hair.
The referee checks with the official behind the goal... and shows red.
Ronaldo can't believe it. He drops to the grass, and walks off in tears.
UEFA gave him a one-match ban. Juventus won anyway, two nil, with ten men.
March twenty twenty-one, Belgrade. Serbia against Portugal, two all, deep in stoppage time.
Ronaldo's shot crosses the line. The replays show it. But there is no VAR, no goal-line technology, and the referee says no goal.
Ronaldo rips off his captain's armband, throws it to the ground, and walks off before the final whistle. He gets a yellow card for his protests.
That night he wrote that he felt an entire nation was being harmed.
And the armband? A stadium worker picked it up, and a charity auctioned it to help pay for surgery for a six-month-old Serbian boy.
Three months later, Belgium knocked Portugal out of the Euros. And the armband hit the floor again.
April twenty twenty-two. Manchester United lose one nil at Everton.
Walking off the pitch, Ronaldo knocks a phone out of a young fan's hand.
He apologised on Instagram for his outburst. Then it got serious.
Police gave him a caution. The FA charged him, rejected his argument that he feared for his safety, and handed him a two-match ban and a fifty thousand pound fine.
Six months later, United beat Tottenham two nil at Old Trafford. Ronaldo is on the bench the whole game.
His manager, Erik ten Hag, says Ronaldo refused to come on. Before the final whistle, Ronaldo walks down the tunnel.
He was dropped for the next game at Chelsea, and told to train away from the squad. A month later, he was gone from Manchester United.
Weeks later he joined Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia. The anger came with him.
March twenty twenty-three. Al Ittihad beat Al Nassr one nil and take top spot. Ronaldo storms off, kicking the water bottles on the touchline.
Rival fans found the button that sets him off. Chanting Messi's name.
In February twenty twenty-four, after a win over Al Shabab, he answered those chants with an obscene gesture. One-match ban, plus a fine.
And against Al Hilal, the rivalry kept getting physical. Weeks after that ban, in a Super Cup semi-final, he threw an elbow at Ali Al-Bulaihi. Straight red. Another two-match ban.
October twenty twenty-four, Hampden Park. Scotland hold Portugal nil nil.
Deep in stoppage time, Portugal are about to take a corner... and the referee blows for full time.
Ronaldo claps sarcastically at the officials, gives a thumbs down, and marches straight to the tunnel.
His post afterwards? Two words. Seguimos juntos. We continue together.
November twenty twenty-five, Dublin. Ireland are beating Portugal two nil in a World Cup qualifier.
Ronaldo elbows defender Dara O'Shea in the back. Red card. His first in two hundred and twenty-six games for Portugal.
He even blamed Ireland's coach for it. The ban could have cost him the start of the World Cup.
Instead, FIFA suspended the rest of the ban for one year. He played the World Cup.
July twenty twenty-six. His sixth, and last, World Cup. Spain knock Portugal out in the round of sixteen, one nil, with a last-gasp goal.
This time, no rage. He said he left with a clear conscience.
Then in September, Portugal's coach Jorge Jesus told him he would not start against Denmark.
Ronaldo left the training camp the day before the game. He said he would tell the Portuguese people the truth about why... later.
Fourteen red cards. Bans, fines, apologies. And still, at forty-one, he wants to play every single minute.
Maybe that's the point. The fire that makes him snap... is the same fire that made him Cristiano Ronaldo.
Which moment was the worst? Tell me in the comments.
